curves.name: harman
curves.title: Harman-style bass shelf
curves.description: First-order low-shelf bass boost with no treble adjustment. The community-standard Dirac target for music.

params.name: shelf_level
params.description: Bass-shelf gain in dB. Typical values: 4-6 for critical listening, 6-8 for balanced music, 10-14 for cinema or bass-heavy use.

params.name: shelf_corner
params.description: Shelf corner frequency in Hz. Higher values extend the shelf into mid-bass for a wider HT-style sound; lower values tighten the shelf to deep bass only.

curves.citation: Olive, S. E. & Welti, T. — Harman International AES research on listener preference for in-room loudspeaker response. See also Toole, F. E., Sound Reproduction (3rd ed., 2017), Routledge / AES Presents.

curves.name: olive_welti_inroom
curves.title: Olive-Welti in-room (RR1_G family)
curves.description: Bass shelf plus linear downward tilt above 1 kHz. Tracks the Olive-Welti-McMullin RR1_G shape.

params.name: bass_shelf
params.description: Low-shelf bass gain in dB. Olive, Welti & McMullin 2013 found preference for ~+6 dB.

params.name: bass_corner
params.description: Low-shelf corner frequency in Hz (≈105 Hz to match the published RR1_G shape).

params.name: treble_tilt
params.description: Linear tilt above the anchor in dB/octave (negative = darker).

params.name: tilt_anchor
params.description: Frequency at which the tilt has 0 dB effect.

curves.citation: Olive, S. E., Welti, T., & McMullin, E. (2013). 'Listener Preferences for In-Room Loudspeaker and Headphone Target Responses.' AES 135th Convention, paper 8994. See also paper 8867 (AES 134th, 2013) for the RR1_G reference curve.

curves.name: b_and_k
curves.title: Brüel & Kjær 1974
curves.description: Flat bass plateau plus linear downward slope above the corner.

params.name: bass_level
params.description: Bass plateau in dB (B&K original ~ 2.5 to 3 dB).

params.name: bass_corner
params.description: Frequency at which the plateau ends and the tilt begins.

params.name: treble_slope
params.description: Downward slope above the bass corner in dB/octave (B&K ≈ -0.83).

curves.citation: Brüel & Kjær Application Note 17-197 (1974), 'Relevant loudspeaker tests in studios in Hi-Fi dealers' demo rooms in the home etc., using 1/3 octave, pink-weighted, random noise.'

curves.name: toole_inroom
curves.title: Toole in-room
curves.description: Flat below ~500 Hz, gentle downward tilt above. Optional bass shelf.

params.name: tilt
params.description: Downward tilt above tilt_corner in dB/octave (Toole: ~ -0.6 to -0.9).

params.name: tilt_corner
params.description: Frequency above which the tilt applies; flat below.

params.name: bass_shelf
params.description: Optional low-shelf bass gain in dB (Toole-neutral default = 0).

params.name: bass_corner
params.description: Low-shelf corner frequency for the optional bass boost.

curves.citation: Toole, F. E. (2017). Sound Reproduction: The Acoustics and Psychoacoustics of Loudspeakers and Rooms (3rd ed.). Routledge / AES Presents.

curves.name: welti_sub
curves.title: Welti subwoofer band
curves.description: Sub-band low-shelf with corner at the crossover frequency.

params.name: shelf_level
params.description: Sub-band low-shelf gain in dB.

params.name: crossover_hz
params.description: Shelf corner frequency, matching your sub-to-mains crossover. Above this frequency the shelf has rolled down toward 0 dB.

curves.citation: Welti, T. & Devantier, A. (2006). 'Low-Frequency Optimization Using Multiple Subwoofers.' J. AES 54(5). See also Welti, 'Subwoofers: Optimum Number and Locations' (Harman International).

curves.name: flat
curves.title: Flat / Unity
curves.description: Zero dB at every frequency. Useful as a baseline before transforms.

curves.name: breakpoints
curves.title: Raw breakpoints
curves.description: User-supplied list of (Hz, dB) pairs interpolated log-linearly.

params.name: points
params.description: List of (freq_hz, gain_db) pairs, strictly sorted by frequency.

transforms.name: gain
transforms.title: Band gain
transforms.description: Add (or subtract) a fixed dB to a band, with cosine-tapered edges.

params.name: low_hz
params.description: Lower edge of the band, in Hz.

params.name: high_hz
params.description: Upper edge of the band, in Hz.

params.name: gain_db
params.description: Gain (positive) or cut (negative) in dB.

params.name: taper
params.description: Edge taper width in octaves (0 = hard rectangular band).

transforms.name: peq
transforms.title: Parametric peak EQ
transforms.description: Bell-shaped peak/cut at a given frequency and Q (RBJ biquad).

params.name: freq
params.description: Center frequency in Hz.

params.name: gain_db
params.description: Peak gain in dB.

params.name: q
params.description: Quality factor: higher = narrower peak.

transforms.name: shelf
transforms.title: Shelf
transforms.description: First-order low or high shelf added on top of the current curve.

params.name: type
params.description: 'low' for bass shelf, 'high' for treble shelf.

params.name: corner
params.description: Shelf corner frequency in Hz.

params.name: gain_db
params.description: Shelf gain in dB.

transforms.name: rolloff
transforms.title: Low-end rolloff
transforms.description: Nth-order Butterworth high-pass magnitude added to the curve.

params.name: freq
params.description: Cutoff frequency in Hz (-3 dB point).

params.name: order
params.description: Butterworth order; 2 is a typical safe default.

transforms.name: tilt
transforms.title: Linear tilt
transforms.description: Linear dB/octave slope across the spectrum, anchored to a chosen Hz.

params.name: db_per_octave
params.description: Tilt slope in dB per octave (negative = darker).

params.name: anchor_hz
params.description: Frequency at which the tilt has zero effect.
